# SN 22.48: Khandha Sutta

*SN 22.48, the Khandha Sutta — set 4, Not-Self and Dependent Arising*

## About this text

This text has not yet been given a reader's introduction. The translation below is the same governed text used throughout the project; only the orienting note is missing.

## The Setting

At Sāvatthī.

"Bhikkhus, I will teach the five heaps and the five clung-to heaps.

Listen to this.

## The Five Heaps

"And what, bhikkhus, are the five heaps?

Whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, coarse
or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near:

this is called the form heap.

Whatever felt experience there is, past, future, or present, internal or
external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near:

this is called the felt-experience heap.

Whatever recognition there is, past, future, or present, internal or external,
coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near:

this is called the recognition heap.

Whatever putting-together activities there are, past, future, or present,
internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near:

this is called the putting-together-activities heap.

Whatever knowing there is, past, future, or present, internal or external,
coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near:

this is called the knowing heap.

These are called the five heaps.

## The Five Clung-To Heaps

"And what, bhikkhus, are the five clung-to heaps?

Whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, coarse
or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, with outflows and fit to be taken
personally:

this is called the form clung-to heap.

Whatever felt experience there is, past, future, or present, internal or
external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, with outflows
and fit to be taken personally:

this is called the felt-experience clung-to heap.

Whatever recognition there is, past, future, or present, internal or external,
coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, with outflows and fit to
be taken personally:

this is called the recognition clung-to heap.

Whatever putting-together activities there are, past, future, or present,
internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, with
outflows and fit to be taken personally:

this is called the putting-together-activities clung-to heap.

Whatever knowing there is, past, future, or present, internal or external,
coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, with outflows and fit to
be taken personally:

this is called the knowing clung-to heap.

These are called the five clung-to heaps."

*[bhikkhus]: Buddhist monks -- those who have left household life to practise full time. The Buddha's usual way of addressing the assembly, roughly "friends" in force.
*[clung-to heaps]: The five categories experience gets sorted into and then grasped as "me" or "mine" -- body, feeling, recognition, mental activity, and awareness. Not clinging to the categories themselves, but to the sense of ownership placed on top of them.
*[felt experience]: This project's rendering of "vedanā" (often translated "feeling") -- the immediate pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral tone of an experience, prior to any story built on top of it.
*[form]: This project's rendering of "rūpa" -- the physical, material aspect of experience, one of the five heaps.
*[heaps]: This project's rendering of "khandhā" (usually translated "aggregates") -- the five piles experience gets sorted into: form, felt experience, recognition, putting-together activities, and knowing.
*[knowing]: This project's rendering of "viññāṇa" (often translated "consciousness") -- bare awareness of an object through one of the senses or the mind.
*[outflows]: This project's rendering of "āsavā" -- deep-running habits that keep seeping out and driving behaviour, classically sensuality, becoming, and ignorance. Often translated "taints" or "defilements."
*[putting-together activities]: This project's rendering of "saṅkhārā" (often translated "mental formations") -- the mind's constructing and assembling activity, one of the five heaps.
*[recognition]: This project's rendering of "saññā" (often translated "perception") -- the mind's act of identifying and labeling what it encounters.
